https://www.advanced-television.com/2026.text: Encompass playout services for Channel 4 July 28, 2026 Encompass Digital Media has been selected by Channel 4, the UK public service broadcasters, to deliver managed linear playout services as part of a new multi-year agreement. The announcement follows a procurement and evaluation process carried out by Channel 4 ahead of the service’s launch in 2027. Under the agreement, Encompass will partner with Channel 4 to provide channel origination, content supply chain and disaster recovery services across its portfolio, including Channel 4, E4, More4, Film4, E4 Extra and 4seven. Encompass will deliver services from its London and Riga broadcast facilities using its cloud-native Altitude platform, including Altitude Playout and Altitude Flow. The deployment is designed to support Channel 4’s broadcast operations through a managed service that combines channel origination with an integrated content supply chain. Encompass’s Altitude platforms take a software-defined, remote-first architectural approach, providing Channel 4 with technical and operational flexibility to navigate the changing playout and distribution landscape. “Channel 4 conducted a rigorous procurement process, and we’re delighted to have been selected as its managed playout partner,” commented Marc Bruce, CEO of Encompass. “This agreement reflects the strength of our technology and our experience supporting leading broadcasters with highly resilient managed services. We look forward to working closely with the Channel 4 team as we prepare for service launch next year.” “We’re pleased to be entering into this new agreement with Encompass,” added Grace Boswood, Director of Technology and Distribution at Channel 4. “Their cloud-native technology and experience supporting modern broadcast environments made them the ideal choice for our future needs, and we look forward to working together.” Other posts by : Arianespace trims ambitions for rocket update Forecast: $5tn annual SpaceX revenues Human AI; Access, Influence Who else was eyeing Globalstar? https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/first-pic.text: Ethan Davies Updated Thu, September 3, 2026 at 4:22 AM UTC 0 Andrea Skopova, aged 20, leaves Sheffield Magistrates Court (Image: Ben Lack Photography Ltd) The suspects accused of murdering a baby girl with 33 wounds in 15 stabbings have been pictured leaving court for the first time. Slovakian nationals Andrea Skopova, 20, Peter Horvath Jnr, 19, Peter Horvath Snr, 38, and Nina Horvathova, 37, are charged with the murder of a newborn named only as Baby S. Tragically, the infant's body was found wrapped in a towel and in a blue bag in an outhouse on Sunday August 30), Sheffield Magistrates Court heard on Wednesday (September 2). Three of the four people accused of murder are also charged with perverting the course of justice, namely Horvath Jnr, Horvath Snr and Horvathova. A 15-year-old girl - who cannot be named for legal reasons - is also charged with perverting the course of justice only. They will all appear at Sheffield Crown Court for the first time on Thursday (September 3). Images show the suspects leaving magistrates' court after a hearing on Wednesday, when prosecutors said the baby's body was found on top of a washing machine in an outhouse at an address in the Wincobank area of Sheffield on Sunday. Baby S was found wrapped in a towel and in a blue bag in an outbuilding at an address in Holywell Heights, they added. Peter Horvath Jnr, aged 19, leaves Sheffield Magistrates Court (Image: Ben Lack Photography Ltd) Horvath Jnr, Horvath Snr and Horvathova, all of Holywell Heights, and Skopova, of Robey Street, Grimesthorpe, Sheffield, are also charged with causing or allowing the death of a child, and perverting the course of justice by cleaning the scene of the alleged crime. On Wednesday, prosecutor Luke Hopkinson told the magistrates' court that the baby's mother is the defendant Andrea Skopova. The father is unknown, Mr Hopkinson said. Skopova is the girlfriend of the defendant Horvath Jnr, who is the son of the other two adult defendants. Mr Hopkinson said Horvath Jnr is not believed to be the father. Mr Hopkinson said Baby S had suffered 33 wounds from 15 "separate stabbings". The prosecutor said she suffered wounds to her "face and torso - front and back". The defendants were remanded in custody to appear at the crown court the following morning. Two women, aged 26 and 37, who were arrested on suspicion of murder remain on bail.
